explain.say: In July 1848, in the small town of Seneca Falls, New York, about three hundred people met to demand women's rights. Their Declaration of Sentiments, led by Elizabeth Cady Stanton, rewrote a famous line to say all men and women are created equal. Its call for the vote was the most controversial part. Look at the timeline of how that demand spread.

explain.say: Now the map. New Zealand came first nationally in 1893, after Kate Sheppard's huge petitions. Finland in 1906 let women vote and stand for parliament. India's 1950 constitution gave every adult the vote at once. Swiss women waited until 1971 for federal votes. What surprises you about who came first and who came last?

draw.label: Votes for women, a world story

explain.say: In Britain there were two wings. See the comparison. Suffragists, led by Millicent Fawcett, used petitions and lobbying. Suffragettes, led by Emmeline Pankhurst, used the slogan deeds not words: smashed windows, arson, and hunger strikes in prison, where many were force-fed. Emily Davison died after running onto the Derby course in 1913. Which method would you choose?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Historians still debate which helped more.

explain.say: Why then? See the causes. Decades of campaigning, women's work in the First World War, new states writing new constitutions, and support from labour and liberal parties. In 1918 British women over 30 who met property rules could vote; equal votes came in 1928. Why might war change how governments see women?

explain.say: The story continues. Women held about 11 percent of parliamentary seats worldwide in 1995 and about 27 percent in 2023; Rwanda leads with over 60. Joan Scott argued in 1986 that gender, the meanings societies give to being women and men, is a key tool of history. Great work. Exam tip: link campaigns to wider political change.

faq.q: Which country first gave women the vote?
faq.a: New Zealand, in September 1893, was the first self-governing country to give all adult women the vote in national elections, after petitions led by Kate Sheppard. Finland in 1906 was the first to let women both vote and stand for parliament.

faq.q: What is the difference between suffragists and suffragettes?
faq.a: In Britain, suffragists, mainly the National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies led by Millicent Fawcett, campaigned peacefully through petitions and lobbying. Suffragettes, the Women's Social and Political Union led by Emmeline Pankhurst, used militant direct action from 1903.

faq.q: Did the First World War win women the vote?
faq.a: It helped. Women's war work changed attitudes, and a 1918 reform was needed anyway for returning soldiers. But decades of campaigning had already built support, and in Britain only women over 30 meeting property rules voted in 1918.
asks: When did British women get the vote?

faq.a: The study of how ideas about being a woman or a man, and the power relations between them, have changed over time. Joan Wallach Scott's 1986 essay called gender a useful category of historical analysis. It includes histories of masculinity too.
